clue.text: Take up summary

blocks.note: first meaning: to begin again after a pause
second meaning: a brief account, as of a career

explanation.walkthrough: Spelt the same, the two senses differ in English only by the accent: one verb, one noun (résumé).
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to continue after interruption, and a résumé is a condensed outline of something.

clue.text: Legal papers read out in luxury hotel

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: writs are formal legal documents issued by a court

explanation.surface: Someone reads out court documents in a plush hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is the famous luxury hotel in London (and elsewhere), a byword for opulence.

clue.text: Say what one has to say — give a speech about it twice

definitions.text: Say what one has to say

indicators.note: about means around, so the speechmaking word goes round the other letters

blocks.note: to spout is to hold forth at length
the word it, written two times

explanation.surface: Advice to a hesitant speaker: get your words out, by speechifying round the subject twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit it out is the idiom urging someone to stop hesitating and say what they mean.

clue.text: The famous steam train — all aboard spoiled on departing

indicators.note: being aboard means being carried inside a vessel, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil
taken as written
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A conductor's call of all aboard for a famous locomotive, spoiled as it pulls away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All aboard' reads as one phrase, but all is the piece and aboard is the signal to put it inside the word for spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallard is the LNER steam locomotive that set the world speed record for steam in 1938.

clue.text: Head of studio's pick, an irresistibly funny person

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of studio
the cream is the pick, the best of a group

explanation.surface: A film studio's boss picks a hilarious performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a scream is the informal idiom for a person who is extremely funny.

clue.text: Financial institution vacating building

blocks.note: clearing a room is vacating it
a house is a building

explanation.surface: A bank moving out of its premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearing house is a financial body that settles transactions between banks or traders.

clue.text: Wayward deserter apprehended by Eric

indicators.note: someone apprehended is held, so one word is gripped inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A wayward deserter is caught by a man called Eric.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is unpredictable and irregular, just as wayward conduct strays from a steady course.

clue.text: Swamp planet with hydrogen

blocks.note: the red planet
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A boggy world rich in hydrogen, like a science-fiction setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh is low, waterlogged land, so it is a synonym for swamp.

clue.text: Experimental process in eastern state — a nation's in fear

indicators.note: the 's stands for is, and is in says one group of letters sits inside another

blocks.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a state on the US East Coast
taken as written
a land is a country or nation
terror is great fear

explanation.surface: A frightened country tests its way forward by experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island, Delaware and the rest are clued as eastern states by their two-letter postal codes; here it is RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial and error is the method of trying options repeatedly until one works, an experimental way of learning.

clue.text: Important zoological area shown in quality book

blocks.note: a thing's nature is its essential quality
to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A key wildlife site featured in a fine book.
explanation.definitionFit: A nature reserve is protected land set aside for wildlife, so it is significant for zoology.

clue.text: Shoot determined and wealthy globetrotters?

blocks.note: to jet is to shoot out in a stream
set on something means determined to do it

explanation.surface: A resolute photographer sets out to shoot rich travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that globetrotters is a loose description of the group, not a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are rich, fashionable people who fly around the world for pleasure.

clue.text: Star dies unexpectedly, causing a catastrophe

indicators.note: unexpectedly means things do not happen in the expected order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A celebrity's sudden death is a tragedy for fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamitous event, a direct synonym for a catastrophe.

clue.text: Volunteers weed a US lake

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
to hoe is to weed with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Volunteers clear weeds around an American lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California–Nevada border.

clue.text: Show off daughter in assembly

blocks.note: to crow is to boast
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A girl showing off at a school assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a large gathering of people, so it is a synonym for an assembly.

clue.text: Oppose doctor in Ulster?

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, the garment wrapping round the doctor

blocks.note: an ulster is a long, heavy overcoat, so it is an example of the general word
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Resisting a medic in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster looks like the Irish province; it is the overcoat named after it, and the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To combat something is to fight or resist it, a synonym for oppose.

clue.text: Unexpectedly meet girl, angry after closing of pier

indicators.note: the closing of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: last letter of pier
Una is a girl's name
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: Bumping into a cross girlfriend at the end of the pier.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the girl and angry words behind the letter from pier.
explanation.definitionFit: To run across someone is the phrasal verb for encountering them by chance.

clue.text: Band in chart rose, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A band unexpectedly climbing the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians, so it is a kind of band.

clue.text: Short court case, in fenland town, for head of family?

indicators.note: something cut short loses its tail, so the final letter goes
in places the shortened word inside the town's name

blocks.note: a trial is a case heard in court
March is a market town in the Cambridgeshire Fens

explanation.surface: A brief court hearing in an East Anglian town for the family's elder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying drained marshland in eastern England; March is one of its towns. The question mark flags that the head must be a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who heads a family, so she is one particular kind of family head.

clue.text: Fail at swimming length? Perhaps never

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so they settle in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot swim a length may never manage it.
explanation.definitionFit: If at all qualifies a statement as possibly not happening, as in 'rarely, if at all', so it hints at never.

clue.text: A Caledonian necktie

blocks.note: taken as written
Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish tie, perhaps in tartan.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neck scarf or cravat worn looped under the chin, a type of tie.

clue.text: Psychiatrist's article on a composer, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the composer is taken by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer and pianist

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist writing a magazine piece about a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is; in a down clue, on puts the article above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst is a psychoanalyst, a therapist who treats the mind; casually a psychiatrist.

clue.text: Greek character in sacred river close to Sparta

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: in Coleridge's Kubla Khan, Alph is 'the sacred river'
last letter of Sparta

explanation.surface: A Greek hero by a holy river near Sparta.
explanation.walkthrough: Alph comes from Coleridge's poem: 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character here means a letter.

clue.text: Appear suddenly from river, followed by young dog

indicators.note: followed by sets the order, putting the young dog after the river

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A puppy bounding out of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop up is the phrasal verb for arriving or showing up without warning.

clue.text: Bangers found by SA customs

blocks.note: taken as written
usages are customary practices

explanation.surface: Fireworks confiscated by South African customs officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers is British slang for sausages, not fireworks here.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is everyday British slang for a sausage, from the way they burst when fried.

clue.text: Edible seaweed brought over in club

indicators.note: something brought over is turned to face the other way, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: nori is the dried seaweed used to wrap sushi

explanation.surface: Imported seaweed served in a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a golf club with a metal head, so it is one kind of club.

clue.text: Hangover cure — fresh air? Yes, I report

indicators.note: something fresh is newly made, so the letters form a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sufferer confirms that fresh air is the cure for a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie oyster is a raw egg swallowed whole with seasoning, a traditional morning-after remedy.

clue.text: Border collie, perhaps, circling tree

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: a collie is an example of a pet
the elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A Border collie running round a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Border collie reads as the dog breed; Border is in fact the definition, and the collie is a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelmet is a narrow border of wood or fabric above a window, hiding the curtain fittings.

clue.text: Mark captures rook, resulting in stress

indicators.note: to capture is to hold within, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a stain is a mark
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess game where a player named Mark takes a rook under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is physical or mental pressure, a direct synonym for stress.
